server_version.markdownDescription: The version of the Metals server artifact. Use `latest-stable` for the latest stable release, `latest-snapshot` for the latest snapshot, or a specific version such as `1.6.9`. Requires restarting Sublime Text.

java_home.markdownDescription: Optional path to the Java home directory used to run the Metals server. When empty, the `JAVA_HOME` environment variable is used, falling back to `java` on the `PATH`. Requires restarting Sublime Text.

server_properties.markdownDescription: Optional list of properties to pass along to the Metals server, for example `-Dhttps.proxyHost=…` or `-Dmetals.statistics=all`. See https://scalameta.org/metals/docs/integrations/new-editor/#metals-server-properties for all properties.

metals.autoImportBuilds.markdownDescription: Automatically import builds rather than prompting the user to choose. `initial` will only automatically import a build when a project is first opened, `all` will automate build imports after subsequent changes as well.

metals.bloopJvmProperties.markdownDescription:
Optional list of JVM properties to pass along to the Bloop server. Each property needs to be a separate item.

Example: `-Xmx1G` or `-Xms100M`

metals.bloopSbtAlreadyInstalled.markdownDescription: If true, Metals will not generate a `project/metals.sbt` file under the assumption that sbt-bloop is already manually installed in the sbt build. Build import will fail with a 'not valid command bloopInstall' error in case Bloop is not manually installed in the build when using this option.

metals.bloopVersion.markdownDescription: This version will be used for the Bloop build tool plugin, for any supported build tool,while importing in Metals as well as for running the embedded server

metals.customProjectRoot.markdownDescription: Optional relative path to your project's root. If you want your project root to be the workspace/workspace root set it to "." .

metals.defaultBspToBuildTool.markdownDescription: Default to using build tool as your build server.

metals.defaultShell.markdownDescription: Optionally provide a default shell executable to use for build operations.

metals.enableBestEffort.markdownDescription: Enable best effort mode for Metals in Scala 3. If enabled, Metals will try to provide most up to date information from the codebase even if it's not compiling.

metals.enableIndentOnPaste.markdownDescription: When this option is enabled, when user pastes any snippet into a Scala file, Metals will try to adjust the indentation to that of the current cursor.

metals.enableSemanticHighlighting.markdownDescription: When this option is enabled, Metals will provide semantic tokens for clients that support it. The feature is still experimental and does not work for all sources.

metals.enableStripMarginOnTypeFormatting.markdownDescription: When enabled, if you press the return key from the first line of a multiline string containing a pipe, it will automatically add `.stripMargin`.

metals.excludedPackages.markdownDescription:
List of packages you'd like to be left out of completions, symbol searches, and code actions.

Ex. `akka.actor.typed.javadsl` will ensure nothing in the `javadsl` package gets recommended to you.

You can find the list of default exclusions [here on the Metals website](https://scalameta.org/metals/docs/editors/user-configuration/#excluded-packages).

If you need to remove one of the defaults, you can simply include it and preface it with `--`.

metals.fallbackScalaVersion.markdownDescription:
The Scala compiler version that is used as the default or fallback in case a file doesn't belong to any build target or the specified Scala version isn't supported by Metals.

This applies to standalone Scala files, worksheets, and Scala CLI scripts.

 The `automatic` value means that the Scala version for these files will be inferred from the highest supported Scala version in your projects build definition

metals.gradleScript.markdownDescription:
Optional absolute path to a `gradle` executable to use for running `gradle bloopInstall`.

By default, Metals uses an embedded `gradlew` script.

Update this setting if your `gradle` script requires more customizations.

metals.inlayHints.byNameParameters.enabl.markdownDescription:
Enable/disable inlay hints for by-name parameters. 
```scala 

 def foo(x: => Int) = ???
 foo(/*=> */1 + 2)
 foo {/*=> */
   val x = 1
   x + 1
 }
```

metals.inlayHints.hintsInPatternMatch.en.markdownDescription:
Enable/disable inlay hints in pattern matches. 
```scala 

 case class Foo(a: Int, b: Int)
 val foo = Foo(1, 2)
 foo match {
   case Foo(a/*: Int*/, b/*: Int*/) =>
 }
```

metals.inlayHints.hintsXRayMode.enable.markdownDescription:
Enable/disable inlay hints for x-ray like mode. 
```scala 

 val finalBar: Bar = foo
  .bar/*  : Bar*/
  .foo()/*: Foo*/
  .bar/*  : Bar*/
```

metals.inlayHints.implicitArguments.enab.markdownDescription:
Enable/disable inlay hints for implicit arguments. 
```scala 

 given bar: Int = 123
 def foo(x: Int)(using Int) = ??? 
 foo(1)/*(using bar)*/
```

metals.inlayHints.implicitConversions.en.markdownDescription:
Enable/disable inlay hints for implicit conversions. 
```scala 

 implicit class MInt(i: Int) {
   def incr: Int = i + 1
 }
 val x = /*MInt(*/1/*)*/.incr 
```

metals.inlayHints.inferredTypes.enable.markdownDescription:
Enable/disable inlay hints for inferred variable types and method return types.
```scala 

 val x/*: List[Int]*/ = List(1)
 def foo(x: Int)/*: Option[Int]*/ = Some(x)
```

metals.inlayHints.namedParameters.enable.markdownDescription:
Enable/disable inlay hints for named parameters. 
```scala 

 def foo(number: Int) = ???
 foo(/*number = */1)
```

metals.inlayHints.typeParameters.enable.markdownDescription:
Enable/disable inlay hints for type parameters. 
```scala 

 val x = List[Int](1)
 def foo[T](x: T) = x
 foo/*[Int]*/(1)
```

metals.javaFormat.eclipseConfigPath.markdownDescription:
Optional custom path to the eclipse-formatter.xml file.

Should be an absolute path and use forward slashes `/` for file separators (even on Windows).

metals.javaFormat.eclipseProfile.markdownDescription: Optional Eclipse format profile to use.

metals.javaHome.markdownDescription:
Optional path to the Java home directory that will be used for compiling the project.

Defaults to JDK used by Metals's server (look: Java Version).

This Java version should be lower or equal to JDK version used by the Metals's server.

metals.mavenScript.markdownDescription:
Optional absolute path to a `mvn` executable to use for running `mvn ch.epfl.scala:maven-bloop_2.10:<bloop_version>:bloopInstall`.

By default, Metals uses an embedded `mvnw` script.

Update this setting if your `mvn` script requires more customizations.

metals.millScript.markdownDescription:
Optional absolute path to a `mill` executable to use for running `mill mill.contrib.Bloop/install`.

By default, Metals uses an embedded `millw` script while respecting `.mill-version` file.

Update this setting if your `mill` script requires more customizations.

metals.sbtScript.markdownDescription:
Optional absolute path to an `sbt` executable to use for running `sbt bloopInstall`.

By default, Metals uses `java -jar sbt-launch.jar` with an embedded launcher while respecting `.jvmopts` and `.sbtopts`.

Update this setting if your `sbt` script requires more customizations like using environment variables.

metals.scalaCliLauncher.markdownDescription: Optional path to Scala CLI launcher to use.

metals.scalafixConfigPath.markdownDescription:
Optional custom path to the .scalafix.conf file.

Should be an absolute path and use forward slashes `/` for file separators (even on Windows).

metals.scalafixLintEnabled.markdownDescription: Enable/disable scalafix linting. If enabled, Metals will lint the codebase using scalafix with the currently defined rules.

metals.scalafixRulesDependencies.markdownDescription: List of Scalafix rules dependencies in case they are not available by default in Metals and running scalafix fails due to 'rule not found' exception. For example: `com.github.liancheng::organize-imports:0.6.0` which follows the [coursier](https://get-coursier.io/) convention.

metals.scalafmtConfigPath.markdownDescription:
Optional custom path to the .scalafmt.conf file.

Should be an absolute path and use forward slashes `/` for file separators (even on Windows).

metals.startMcpServer.markdownDescription: If Metals should start an HTTP Model Context Protocol server, that can be used by AI tools to provide better context about the codebase. Needs to be enabled in the client as well.

metals.superMethodLensesEnabled.description: Enable/disable goto super method code lens.

metals.testEnvironmentVariables.markdownDescription: Optional environment variables to pass to tests. Each key-value pair should be a separate item.

metals.verboseCompilation.markdownDescription: If a build server supports it (for example Bloop or Scala CLI), setting it to true will make the logs contain all the possible debugging information including that about incremental compilation in Zinc.
